title: How to Read a 10-K Report Without Reading Every Page
summary: How to read a 10-K item by item: what Business, Risk Factors, MD&A, financial statements and footnotes tell you, what to skip, and how students and sales teams can use it.
body_markdown:
Read the 10-K for the full-year picture and the 10-Q for what happened since. The SEC's[EDGAR guide](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-search-assistance/using-edgar-research-investments) describes the 10-K as the annual report with audited financial statements, and the 10-Q as the quarterly report with unaudited financial statements and updates on risks and results. Material events between reports appear in Form 8-K, and executive pay usually sits in the proxy statement (DEF 14A).


The reading order above works for a 10-Q too: it has its own MD&A, financial statements and risk-factor updates, just shorter and covering a quarter. Quarterly numbers are easier to read next to the earnings release; our guide on[reading an earnings report](https://meetbenson.com/blog/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) covers that side.
